title: Tenant-islanded upgrade strategy with soft-drain and autoscaler contracts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: We need an upgrade workflow for Dedicated GPU pools that minimizes customer impact during LTS channel rollouts and security/OS/kernel patching. Existing drain-orchestration approaches cause tenant-wide traffic bursts and autoscaler thrashing when multiple pools run concurrent drains. Goal: implement a tenant-islanded upgrade strategy that isolates tenant work, uses a "soft-drain" phase that prefers eviction-free handoff, and formalizes an autoscaler contract to prevent surge oscillation. Scope: upgrade controller changes, autoscaler API extension, rollout gate definitions, canary instrumentation, runbook updates, and e2e upgrade tests on staging clusters. Out of scope: new billing model changes, node image build pipeline (handled elsewhere).
acceptance_criteria: Controller can mark a pool in islanded mode and perform soft-drain that avoids evicting in-use slots for 95% of affected requests under median load
Autoscaler contract implemented: scaling decisions respect a cooling window and reserved tenant quotas during upgrades
Canary rollout gate: metrics based gate (p99 latency, error-rate, token cost delta) evaluated automatically and able to abort or pause rollout
Runbook and rollback steps documented and validated in a tabletop with SRE and Product
Staging can run full fleet upgrade simulation with representative tenant mixes without violating SLOs for more than 30 minutes
updates: 2025-02-18: Ticket created after postmortem for 2025-02-12 upgrade spike. Initial rough design sketched; creator: Maya Chen.

2025-02-20: Architecture review with runtime, autoscaler, and SRE. Agreed on three-phase flow: quiesce->soft-drain->hard-drain. Decided soft-drain should attempt KV cache prefetching and live-migration of warm slots where possible. Action: LUCR-PR#112 to prototype soft-drain signaling.

2025-02-24: Autoscaler contract draft posted. Key points: (1) scaler exposes plannedDrain(tag, capacityReserve) endpoint; (2) drain requests include tenant-affinity signals; (3) scaler will not scale down below reserved capacity for drain duration plus grace window. Feedback from autoscale owners (Priya Patel): reduce reserve default from 20% to 10% to avoid wasted capacity on low-util tiers. Updated contract in design doc.

2025-02-26: Prototype merged to staging (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1347). Soft-drain now emits a Tenant-Island event and sets per-tenant reservation metadata on pool objects. Initial load tests show 8% latency tail increase during mixed workloads; within acceptable threshold but needs tuning for GPU-bound inference shapes. Assigned follow-up to GPU kernel team.

2025-02-28: Canary gating rules finalized: abort if p99 latency regresses >15% for 10 minutes or error rate >0.5% absolute. Added cost delta check: token-per-inference change >8% triggers manual review. PM review (Omar Singh) requested explicit operator override and telemetry retention for 14 days. Added to runbook.

2025-03-01: Staging run completed with tenant-mix simulation. Observed autoscaler thrash in scenario with heavy bursty tenants; root cause: scaler cooldown was being reset by drain plan flips. Mitigation agreed: introduce immutable drain plan id and require scaler cooldown to be anchored to plan start. Filing follow-up ENG-88454 to update scaler implementation.
notes: Trade-offs: soft-drain reduces evictions but increases time-to-complete upgrades. We prioritize tenant QoE over rollout speed for LTS and security patches.
Open question: whether to expose per-tenant upgrade windows to customers (opt-in). PM wants this data for enterprise customers but it may complicate scheduling logic.
Related incident: 2025-02-12 spike postmortem linked in Confluence doc; this design is targeted at preventing recurrence.
